1 R/CR.A/1379/2005 JUDGMENT registered against the respondents-accused for the offence punishable under Sections-16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act for the breach of Sections-2(i-a)(a), 2(i-a)(m), 2(ix)(d) and 7(i), 7(ii) and 7(v) of the PFA Act and Rules-29 and 5(A-05-05-01) of the PFA Rules.

[2] According to the prosecution case, on 04.02.1995, complainant Food Inspector Shri S.A.Patel,
visited the place of respondent-accused, who was found dealing with commodities.

It is further the case of the prosecution that complainant Food Inspector purchased sample of 600 grams Chilly Powder (loose) from the respondent-accused on making payment of cost and sent it to Public Analyst, Vadodara for the purpose of analysis.

On receipt of the report from the public analysis, the said sample was found substandard because of the fact that pink and orange coloured oil soluble coaltar colour as well as presence of characteristic debris of chilly powder were found.
As a result of which, a complaint was filed against the respondent-accused for the alleged offence as stated above before the Court of learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Malia Hatina.

sentences.text: Thereafter, summons was issued to respondent-accused.
Then charge-sheet was filed before the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Malia Hatina, which was numbered as Criminal Case No.187 of 1995.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: [3] On the basis of above allegations, charge was framed and read-over and explained to the accused for the offence punishable under Sections-16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act for the breach of Sections-2(i-a)(a), R/CR.A/1379/2005 JUDGMENT 2(i-a)(m), 2(ix)(d) and 7(i), 7(ii) and 7(v) of the PFA Act and Rules-29 and 5(A-05-05-01) of the PFA Rules.
Then, plea vide was recorded and respondent-accused pleaded not guilty to the charge and claimed to be tried.

[4] In support of the prosecution case, prosecution has examined oral evidences:-

Vadodara at Exh.16, acknowledgment receipt at Exh.18, letter from Local Health Authority,

letter to complainant by helper at Exh.21, report of public analyst at Exh.22, letter of sanction at Exh.23, order to file complaint of Food Commissioner to complainant at Exh.24, letter of the complainant to Assistant Commissioner, Junagadh stating to file complaint at Exh.25, letter of Assistant Commissioner, Junagadh for reanalysis of the respondent-accused at Exh.26,

He further admitted that he was innocent and he has not committed any offence.
[7] Then, arguments of both the parties were heard.

After considering the defence version of the respondents- accused, the learned trial Judge observed that prosecution did not follow the mandatory provision of law and microscopic test is not permissible in eye of law.
In result of breach of the provision of law, learned trial Judge acquitted the respondent-accused from the alleged charge levelled against him.
[8] Heard Ms.Hansa Punani, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the appellant-State and Mr.R.C.Kakkad, learned counsel for respondent-accused.

[9] Ms.Hansa Punani, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the appellant-State read the evidence of the complainant at Exh.9 and documents at Exh.10 to 27 and contended that as per the evidence of the complainant, he is a public servant and question of health and larger interest of the society is involved in the present case.
She contended that only on the technical ground, learned trial chose the short cut and acquitted the respondent-accused from the alleged serious charge.
R/CR.A/1379/2005 JUDGMENT

From the evidence of panch Chhaganbhai Kanjibhai at Exh.37,
contents of the panchnama gets substantiated, but the learned trial Judge committed a grave error and wrongly acquitted the respondent-accused from the alleged charge.

[10] Mr.R.C.Kakkad, learned counsel for respondent- accused drew attention to test followed by the prosecution and vehemently argued that our legislations does not permit to follow the microscopic test, whereas in present case, it is admitted by the complainant himself that microscopic test was followed.
He further contended that evidence of the complainant himself shows that mandatory provision of law under Rules-14 and 16 of the PFA Rules, is not followed.

He read the cross-examination of the complainant and further argued that it appears that, the complainant did not come with the clean hand as he could not able to produce any cogent evidence in support of the prosecution case.

He relied upon the decision of this Court in the case of Gangadhar Yashwant Ramekar v/s. Mukeshbhai B. Shah and others, reported in, 1999(1) GLH 237, wherein, it is laid down that Rule-14 is mandatory and in absence of personal knowledge or information of the complainant, as to whether the bottles in which the sample were taken were clean or not.

entities.text: Gangadhar Yashwant Ramekar v/s. Mukeshbhai B. Shah and others, reported in, 1999(1) GLH 237
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In that nature, when rule is mandatory, would vitiate the proceedings.
He further submitted that judgment and order of the learned trial Judge is required to be confirmed.
R/CR.A/1379/2005 JUDGMENT [11] I have perused the submission made by the learned counsel for the parties.
The complainant, in cross- examination, created certain doubt as to whether he visited the shop of the respondent-accused or not.
One hand, he stated that he visited the place in presence of panch and he purchased chilly powder and issued receipt to that effect to the respondent-accused.
On other hand, he admitted in cross-examination that he did not enter into the shop of the respondent-accused.
He further disclosed that microscopic test was followed by him.
As laid down by this Court, microscopic test is not permissible in eye of law.

In present case, evidence of the complaint creates doubt and learned trial Judge reasonably observed and considered that the State Of Gujarat vs Kishorbhai Gordhanbhai ... on 9 April, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75473114/
3 prosecution could not prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.

sentences.text: I am of the opinion that when mandatory provision of law is not followed by the prosecution, then judgment and order of the acquittal passed by the learned trial Judge, is required to be confirmed and therefore, present appeal deserves to be dismissed.
[12] In view of the above, the present Appeal is hereby dismissed.

The impugned judgment and order dated 11.09.2004 rendered by the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Maliya Hatina, in Criminal Case No.187 of 1995, acquitting the respondent-accused is hereby confirmed.
Record and proceedings, if any, be sent back to the trial Court concerned, forthwith.
Bail bond shall stand cancelled.
R/CR.A/1379/2005 JUDGMENT

(Z.K.SAIYED, J.)
